reconcile.connective: Defenders argue the texts equivocate on "fear": Scripture commands filial, reverential fear of God, while the "no fear" verses cast out only the slavish dread of punishment.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells catalogues this as a standing contradiction, holding that 1 John uses "fear" in its ordinary sense and that redefining it as mere reverence is special pleading rather than what the texts say.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible ("Should we fear God?")
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013), "Should we fear God?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: There is a slavish fear of God, springing from hard thoughts of him, which is contrary to religion, Mat 25:24. There is a selfish fear of God springing from dreadful thoughts of him, which may be a good step towards religion, Act 9:5. But there is a filial fear of God, springing from great and high thoughts of him, which is the life and soul of all religion.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the tension by distinguishing kinds of fear: the slavish fear (which the NT casts out) versus the filial fear that is commanded. The clearest both-true harmonization on the row.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Godly fear of offending God is quite distinct from slavish fear of consciously deserved punishment. The latter fear is natural to us all until love casts it out.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Applies the distinction directly to the contested verse: 1 John 4:18 removes slavish fear of punishment, not the godly fear of offending God that the OT commands.

excerpts.excerpt_text: …not the filial fear of God, the new covenant grace of fear, which is the beginning of wisdom, and is consistent with faith, hope, love, and spiritual joy; but either the fear of men, which brings a snare …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: On the contested verse, Gill specifies that the fear cast out is not the commanded filial fear of God but a lesser fear (of men / of judgment), so the verses address different objects.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-14)
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry treats this passage directly, distinguishing slavish, selfish, and filial fear of God (on Job 28:20) and separating the commanded fear of God from being afraid of him (on 1 John 4:17).
